goal: Turn the structurally separated Agent package into a headless runtime with pure host ports and no Flutter or Vityo dependencies.
description: Scope: products/vityo_coding_agent entrypoint, application/session boundary, host ports, controlled headless host, package exports, and smoke tests; removal of moved monolithic controller/context facades owned by this closure. Context: the atomic cutover establishes final roots but preserves behavior; current controller extends Flutter ChangeNotifier and context imports concrete IDE services. Target: the Agent library and CLI initialize, run, cancel, complete, and fail deterministically against an in-memory host without Vityo; UI notification becomes an outer projection concern; every host interaction crosses a typed port. Design Considerations: decompose by state owner, keep pure application code inward of adapters, use explicit cancellation/deadline objects, and delete old concrete-controller forwarding APIs after call sites migrate. Design Value: every provider, context, tool, recovery, and multi-agent capability can now be tested independently of the IDE. Constraints & Risks: no temporary Flutter dependency, service locator, direct filesystem access, or compatibility facade may remain.

symbols.signature: typed facts, tools, roots, change proposals, and receipts

interfaces.name: HostWorkspace
interfaces.inputs: bounded typed host requests with roots, revisions, deadlines, and cancellation
interfaces.outputs: revisioned facts, effect/change receipts, and explicit capability failures

dependencies.reason: The runtime consumes neutral wire DTOs at its outer adapter only.

decisions.composition: A pure AgentRuntime composes application services from host/provider/store/policy ports; CLI and protocol are outer adapters.
decisions.algorithms: Session commands reduce through an explicit state machine with bounded cancellation and deadline checks.
decisions.data_structures: Immutable command/event types and maps keyed by task/session IDs replace widget-owned mutable lists.
decisions.state: One application service owns each session; adapters own transports; hosts own external resources.
decisions.isolation: Dependency checks forbid Flutter, Vityo, ambient filesystem, and IDE data-store imports.
decisions.concurrency: Each session has a serialized command queue; independent sessions may run concurrently.

acceptance_criteria.text: The pure Dart Agent library and CLI start, complete, cancel, and return structured failure exit codes against an in-memory host with Vityo absent.
Resolved dependency inspection finds no Flutter, Vityo, direct IDE controller/store, ambient filesystem, or retired compatibility API in the Agent product.

goal: Deliver a provider-neutral streamed model runtime with explicit capabilities, budgets, cancellation, retry safety, and usage receipts.
description: Scope: Agent provider ports/adapters, message and tool-call streaming, routing, budgets, cancellation, timeouts, retry/idempotency classification, usage receipts, and deterministic provider fixtures. Context: existing provider behavior is concentrated in a multi-thousand-line adapter/controller path and provider fallback can be unsafe if it cannot distinguish pre-effect generation from post-effect continuation. Target: one vendor-neutral contract normalizes capabilities, chunks, tool calls, structured failures, and usage; routing chooses only compatible providers; cancellation and budgets terminate promptly; fallback never replays a committed mutation. Design Considerations: parse streams incrementally, use a bounded state machine per request, classify failures before retry, and keep vendor DTOs in adapters. Design Value: model choice becomes configuration rather than architecture and cost/latency remain observable. Constraints & Risks: no raw credentials in config/events, no unbounded chunk accumulation, and no automatic retry after an uncertain effect boundary.

interfaces.name: ModelProvider
interfaces.inputs: normalized messages, selected tools, output budget, deadline, cancellation, idempotency boundary
interfaces.outputs: incremental text/tool events, usage, finish reason, and structured failure

decisions.composition: Vendor adapters implement one provider port; router and stream reducer remain vendor-neutral.
decisions.algorithms: Incremental stream reduction and capability filtering avoid buffering full responses; retry uses failure and effect classification.
decisions.data_structures: Immutable capability sets, route candidates, bounded chunk buffers, and usage counters.
decisions.state: One request reducer owns stream state; router owns health projections; secret adapters own credentials.
decisions.isolation: Vendor request/response types and credentials do not enter orchestration or durable session events.
decisions.concurrency: Cancellation/deadlines race safely with stream completion; provider concurrency obeys per-route limits.

acceptance_criteria.text: Provider contract tests cover capabilities, fragmented text/tool streams, usage receipts, cancellation, timeout, auth/rate-limit failures, and context/output budget exhaustion.
Routing and retry tests prove compatible provider selection, safe failover before effects, and refusal to replay an uncertain or committed mutation.

commit.message: agent: add provider-neutral streamed model runtime

goal: Build a revisioned, provenance-bearing, incremental context engine with deterministic relevance and bounded memory/token cost.
description: Scope: context evidence model, source adapters, candidate retrieval, scoring, deduplication, budget packing, conversation compaction, revision invalidation, redaction, caches, metrics, fixtures, and benchmarks. Context: the current Agent session context is roughly 7,600 lines and eagerly couples many IDE domains into one snapshot; this makes another client impossible and encourages repeated serialization. Target: context is requested from host sources, selected per task/step, tied to revisions and provenance, and packed deterministically under explicit byte/token/sensitivity budgets; updates invalidate only affected entries; hot memory remains bounded. Design Considerations: maps and stable digests handle dedupe, bounded LRU caches materialized content, interval indexes handle ranges, and a stable scoring/tie-break policy keeps tests reproducible. Design Value: relevant evidence improves coding accuracy while incremental selection reduces latency and memory. Constraints & Risks: never trust stale facts, include excluded/secrets by accident, rescan the whole workspace on each turn, or hide truncation.

interfaces.name: ContextSource
interfaces.inputs: task/step query, roots, expected revisions, source cap, cancellation
interfaces.outputs: paged context evidence candidates with provenance and cost

dependencies.reason: Context sources query host facts without importing IDE implementation.

decisions.composition: Independent lazy context sources feed one deterministic ranking and budget-packing pipeline.
decisions.algorithms: Hard inclusions, revision filtering, stable dedupe, weighted scoring, deterministic tie-breaks, and greedy capped packing.
decisions.data_structures: Stable-ID maps, digest sets, range indexes, bounded LRU caches, and immutable evidence pages.
decisions.state: Sources own retrieval indexes; cache owns materialized content; engine owns only one selection operation.
decisions.isolation: Root and sensitivity checks happen before materialization/provider exposure.
decisions.concurrency: Independent sources query concurrently under a deadline; merge/ranking is deterministic and cancellation-aware.

acceptance_criteria.text: Context fixtures prove deterministic relevance, provenance, revision invalidation, deduplication, source caps, visible truncation, redaction, and deterministic conversation compaction.
The large-workspace benchmark meets documented latency and memory budgets, shows bounded cache eviction, and performs no unconditional whole-workspace rescan per turn.

commit.message: agent: add incremental revisioned context engine

goal: Deliver the schema-first built-in/MCP tool runtime and enforce roots, permissions, hooks, network, secrets, and effect receipts outside model control.
description: Scope: tool descriptors/registry/discovery, MCP client, executor, schema and result validation, task relevance filter, risk/effect classifier, roots, permissions, grants/revocation, hooks, network and secret policy, audit receipts, cancellation, and security/conformance fixtures. Context: existing tool and permission models are useful but run inside the IDE controller and do not implement MCP roots, dynamic removal, audience-bound secrets, or a single enforceable effect pipeline. Target: built-in and MCP tools follow one bounded typed lifecycle; only relevant/current tools reach the provider; every effect is policy checked at execution time; denied/revoked actions fail closed; outputs are bounded, redacted, scanned, and treated as untrusted evidence. Design Considerations: immutable versioned catalogs, exact-ID maps plus compiled path/network matchers, idempotency keys, pre/post hooks, and explicit permission scope. Design Value: safe autonomy depends more on the effect boundary than model instructions. Constraints & Risks: read-only annotations cannot authorize; prevent traversal, symlink escape, token passthrough, confused-deputy credentials, output flooding, and hook bypass.

interfaces.name: ToolExecutor
interfaces.inputs: validated tool call, current catalog version, roots, policy, permission callback, deadline, cancellation
interfaces.outputs: bounded redacted result and idempotent effect/audit receipt

dependencies.reason: Every tool effect passes policy, roots, permission, secret, network, and hook enforcement.

decisions.composition: Catalog/discovery, policy evaluation, execution adapter, hooks, and receipt writer are separate stages in one effect pipeline.
decisions.algorithms: Schema validation and exact-ID lookup precede compiled root/path/network matching and ordered hook evaluation.
decisions.data_structures: Immutable descriptor maps, versioned root/grant sets, compiled rule matchers, and append-only effect receipts.
decisions.state: Catalog, policy snapshot, grant store, and individual execution each have one owner and version.
decisions.isolation: Models cannot invoke adapters directly; credentials are opaque and resolved only for the intended executor/audience.
decisions.concurrency: Per-effect idempotency and cancellation are enforced; catalog/policy snapshots are immutable during one execution.

acceptance_criteria.text: Built-in and MCP conformance tests prove schema validation, relevance filtering, dynamic discovery/removal, result limits, cancellation, timeout, and server-loss behavior.

Adversarial tests prove traversal/symlink, revoked grants, destructive/process/network denial, secret audience binding, no token passthrough, hook enforcement, redaction, and idempotent audit receipts.

commit.message: agent: enforce schema-first tools and execution policy

goal: Implement the bounded evidence-driven coding loop that plans, edits through host transactions, verifies facts, repairs safely, and reports blockers.
description: Scope: task understanding, plan/step model, prerequisite readiness, plan-act-observe-verify-repair state machine, change-set proposals, focused validation selection, post-edit fact refresh, repair/duplicate-failure guards, user steering, and reference coding fixtures. Context: current code has plan and tool-loop types but orchestration is embedded in a large controller and can treat provider prose as progress; a real Coding Agent needs explicit acceptance and effect boundaries. Target: representative bug-fix and refactor tasks produce scoped plans, approved revisioned change sets, refreshed diagnostics/tests, and evidence-backed completion; cancellation/steering works between transitions; repeated failures stop with a truthful blocker. Design Considerations: immutable plans with a ready queue, explicit budgets, effect receipts, deterministic guard keys, and host facts as the source of verification. Design Value: this is the independently acceptable coding capability, while providers/context/tools remain replaceable services. Constraints & Risks: no direct file writes through the IDE host, no self-reported validation, no unbounded repair, and no unrelated task expansion.

symbols.signature: immutable steps, prerequisites, ownership, acceptance, tools, and budgets

interfaces.name: CodingLoop
interfaces.inputs: goal, current session, provider/context/tool/host ports, budgets, cancellation, steering
interfaces.outputs: plan/step events, change sets, validation receipts, completion or blocker

dependencies.reason: The loop obtains structured model events through the neutral provider port.
Each loop transition requests bounded revisioned evidence.
All observations and effects use the enforced tool pipeline.

decisions.composition: An explicit loop coordinates replaceable provider, context, tool, host, and receipt ports.
decisions.algorithms: Prerequisite-ready step selection, bounded state transitions, refreshed fact verification, and repeated-failure fingerprints control progress.
decisions.data_structures: Immutable plan DAG, ready priority queue, step/effect maps, and bounded failure fingerprint counters.
decisions.state: CodingLoop owns transition state; host owns workspace truth; provider/tool/context services own no plan state.
decisions.isolation: Each task step declares ownership and effects; change sets stay uncommitted until host review/transaction.
decisions.concurrency: A single task loop serializes mutating steps; independent read observations may run concurrently under one cancellation tree.

acceptance_criteria.text: Reference bug-fix and refactor fixtures produce independently reviewable plans, revisioned change sets, focused validation receipts, and evidence-backed completion through host transactions.

Cancellation, steering, stale revisions, denied capabilities, repeated identical failures, budget limits, and failed validation terminate or repair within explicit bounds and surface truthful blockers.

goal: Make Coding Agent sessions durable, crash-recoverable, correlated, redacted, and idempotent at every effect boundary.
description: Scope: append-only session events, compact projections, checkpoints, idempotency/effect receipts, recovery, corruption handling, bounded hot windows, observability correlation, redaction, migration from mixed history/snapshot stores, and crash fixtures. Context: current history, checkpoint, workspace snapshot, tool journal, and controller state are separate large structures; a process boundary and asynchronous work require one durable ordering model. Target: goals, turns, plans, steps, tool calls, permissions, changes, validations, budgets, and outcomes survive restart; recovery replays from the last committed sequence; an effect already receipted is never repeated; corrupted tails preserve and expose the valid prefix. Design Considerations: append immutable events with monotonic per-session sequence and idempotency keys, checkpoint compact projections, and keep raw content outside operational logs. Design Value: users can trust long tasks and audit what happened even after failure. Constraints & Risks: no raw secrets, unbounded event replay, partial checkpoint overwrite, or best-effort duplicate mutation.

interfaces.name: SessionEventStore
interfaces.inputs: expected sequence, immutable redacted events, idempotency/effect receipts

dependencies.reason: Every durable loop transition and effect boundary emits a correlated session event.

decisions.composition: Append-only events are canonical; compact projections and checkpoints are disposable read optimizations.
decisions.algorithms: Optimistic sequence append, checkpoint-plus-tail replay, digest verification, and idempotency lookup prevent lost or duplicate effects.
decisions.data_structures: Ordered immutable events, sequence-indexed segments, compact ID maps, bounded hot deques, and idempotency receipt maps.
decisions.state: Event store owns durable order; projection owns derived current state; adapters own storage transactions.
decisions.isolation: Sessions have independent logs/checkpoints and redaction occurs before persistence/log export.
decisions.concurrency: One writer per session sequence; independent sessions append concurrently; conflicts reload and retry only non-effect state transitions.

acceptance_criteria.text: Kill/restart and replay fixtures recover task/session state from a committed checkpoint and valid event tail with bounded hot memory and correlated redacted receipts.
Effects at every crash boundary execute at most once, while corrupted tails or digest/sequence conflicts preserve valid history and produce explicit recoverable/blocked outcomes.

commit.message: agent: add durable event-sourced session recovery

goal: Deliver real multi-agent delegation with dependency-aware scheduling, isolated worktrees, scoped policy/context, resource leases, and reviewed integration.
description: Scope: task DAG, role/scoped Agent descriptors, ready scheduler, concurrency limits, cancellation tree, worktree provider, resource leases, worker sessions, result collection, conflict detection, reviewed integration, cleanup, and parallel fixtures. Context: current primary/subagent registry metadata does not execute delegated work or prevent ownership collisions. Target: a coordinator delegates independently acceptable steps to isolated worker sessions, runs only ready non-conflicting work within budgets, propagates cancellation, collects evidence/change sets deterministically, and presents integration/conflicts instead of silently merging. Design Considerations: adjacency lists plus indegree counts and a deterministic priority queue make readiness efficient; a normalized resource lease map prevents conflicting mutation; one worktree per mutating worker isolates files. Design Value: parallelism reduces latency only when independence and integration are explicit. Constraints & Risks: no shared mutable context, ambient branch mutation, hidden merge, orphaned worktree, unlimited fan-out, or worker permission widening.

interfaces.name: WorktreeProvider
interfaces.inputs: base revision, worker ID, normalized ownership scope, cancellation
interfaces.outputs: isolated workspace handle, change set, cleanup receipt

dependencies.reason: Each delegated worker is an isolated durable session with correlated parent/child events.

decisions.composition: Coordinator combines a task graph, deterministic scheduler, worker session factory, lease registry, worktree provider, and reviewed integration plan.
decisions.algorithms: Adjacency lists and indegree counts feed a priority-ready queue; semaphore and resource leases bound safe concurrency.
decisions.data_structures: Task DAG maps, indegree counters, priority heap, normalized scope-to-lease map, and parent/child session index.
decisions.state: Scheduler owns task lifecycle; lease registry owns ownership; worktree provider owns isolated filesystem resources.
decisions.isolation: Workers receive scoped context/tools/budgets and distinct worktrees; integration occurs only through reviewable change sets.
decisions.concurrency: Ready non-conflicting tasks run up to one configured semaphore limit; cancellation propagates and releases resources.

acceptance_criteria.text: Parallel fixtures prove dependency-ready scheduling, configured concurrency, isolated context/tools/budgets/worktrees, deterministic evidence collection, cancellation propagation, and cleanup.
Overlapping resource scopes cannot execute concurrently, and worker changes are never silently merged: clean integration and conflicts both produce reviewable plans and receipts.

goal: Ship the interoperable Agent-side protocol endpoint and freeze a reproducible release evaluation corpus against Vityo.
description: Scope: Agent-side shared-protocol adapter, stdio endpoint, initialization/capability negotiation, concurrent session routing, permission/elicitation/cancellation, dynamic capabilities, MCP attachment, unsupported-version behavior, real Vityo integration fixture, deterministic evaluation corpus, and quality budgets. Context: independent modules do not prove that a user can launch the real Agent from the IDE or that quality/security remain measurable across releases. Target: Vityo Coding Agent interoperates through the neutral ACP-compatible boundary without object sharing, serves two sessions, completes a reviewed coding fixture, and exposes reproducible task/security/latency/memory/cancellation evaluation inputs for final validation. Design Considerations: keep protocol translation at the edge, correlate every event, version fixtures/schema digests, and assert final repository facts rather than model prose. Design Value: the Agent becomes a real attachable product with an objective release contract. Constraints & Risks: no private IDE imports, hidden fallback protocol, live credential dependency, nondeterministic acceptance, or green result when a required capability is absent.

A versioned deterministic release corpus covers task quality, allowed effects, security, cancellation, latency, memory, and unsupported capabilities with machine-checkable final facts and budgets.

goal: Make the Coding Agent full validation harness always emit a bounded diagnostic receipt before product suites can be accepted.
description: Closure: capability - Coding Agent full validation receipt reliability; Enabling work: this validation-only repair supports the final REQ-AGENT evidence node without claiming a product requirement. Context: the first formal full entry returned before any suite and emitted no receipt. Target: the harness records stable per-requirement outcomes and a bounded failure code on every exit path without executing suites in its own focused tests. Design Considerations: inject runner callables in acceptance, atomically write receipts, and never expose captured runtime output. Design Value: final validation failures become attributable without rerunning blindly. Constraints & Risks: no product implementation changes, no full-suite execution, and no raw exception or machine data in receipts.

decisions.composition: One receipt boundary wraps the fixed nine-suite plan.
decisions.data_structures: Nine requirement outcome records and bounded digests.
decisions.state: The harness owns only validation receipt state.
decisions.isolation: Focused acceptance injects no-op and failing runners.

acceptance_criteria.text: Injected pass and failure fixtures both emit bounded receipts with exactly REQ-AGENT-001 through REQ-AGENT-009 and never invoke the real full suites.

goal: Run the Vityo Coding Agent full regression exactly once and record independent evidence for REQ-AGENT-001 through REQ-AGENT-009.
description: Scope: validation and evidence recording only; source defects return to their owning implementation lifecycle. Context: focused suites prove modules, while release acceptance must prove one standalone and IDE-attached product across providers, context, tools/policy, coding-loop tasks, crash recovery, parallel worktrees, security, and budgets on one commit. Target: execute Validation.md's coding-agent/full suite once, record schema/fixture/platform/content digests and one outcome per requirement, then sync and validate Better Plan state. Design Considerations: use deterministic fake providers and controlled hosts for the release floor; exercise the real IDE/Agent process boundary without rerunning the IDE full suite. Design Value: objective task/effect facts replace accumulated unit claims or natural-language self-assessment. Constraints & Risks: missing fixtures, skipped adversarial cases, unavailable protocol integration, or exceeded budgets are blocked/failing outcomes; final validation does not implement repairs.

dependencies.reason: The fixed full-suite receipt supplies final requirement evidence.

decisions.composition: Final validation aggregates frozen focused contracts and executes one Coding Agent-wide suite.
decisions.algorithms: Checks and deterministic evaluation cases run once in a fixed order on one head commit.
decisions.data_structures: Per-requirement/case receipts retain outcome, allowed effects, budgets, schema, fixture, artifact, and content digests.
decisions.state: Only this lifecycle may mark the full Coding Agent line validated.
decisions.isolation: The real IDE integration uses the protocol boundary; IDE full regression is not repeated.
decisions.concurrency: No implementation overlaps the full run and parallel fixtures use controlled worktrees/concurrency.

acceptance_criteria.text: The one coding-agent/full suite passes on one head commit and records a traceable outcome for every REQ-AGENT-* label, including headless use, security, crash recovery, parallel worktrees, real IDE integration, and all budgets.
The canonical Better Plan status sync, workspace validation, and requirement-label checker pass with final evidence attached and no implementation work left in the Coding Agent plan.
